scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4535: HELP!! The two departments have been CUT OFF from each
other!! From the department head's machine, none of the computers in the other
department answer any more -- our own department is fine, it's just the other
one that's gone. Something that joins the two departments must be wrong, but I
don't know what. Could someone look at it and rejoin the departments!!!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. router0 connects IT (192.168.1.0/24) and CS
  (192.168.2.0/24) and routes between them; it_hod reaches CS hosts (192.168.2.x)
  with 0% loss. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of an inter-department routing fault that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- IT (192.168.1.x) cannot
reach CS (192.168.2.x) -- is NOT reproducible: router0's IT and CS interfaces
(192.168.1.1 / 192.168.2.1) are up, ripd is running, and it_hod reaches
192.168.2.x with 0% loss.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: inter-department routing is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the IT->CS path,
finds it working, checks router0's interfaces and RIP/connected routes, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a dropped interface or a missing route to
satisfy the ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
A full four-phase diagnostic sweep was performed across the entire Kath2 topology in response to helpdesk ticket #4535, which claimed the IT and CS departments were completely cut off from one another.

**Affected component:** None identified. All subsystems are healthy.

**Mechanism:** Both departments connect via a single router — router0 — which has direct Layer-3 interfaces into each department LAN: eth0 carries 192.168.1.0/24 (IT, via switch0) and eth1 carries 192.168.2.0/24 (CS, via switch1). Router0's routing table correctly lists both subnets as directly connected, so inter-department traffic needs only one hop.

**Localization:** Direct probes confirmed 0% packet loss in both directions across all tested host pairs: cs_hod↔it_hod and cs_hod↔it_lab1 and it_hod↔cs_lab1. All four inter-department paths returned replies with TTL=63, consistent with a single router hop through router0.

**Evidence against an intermittent fault:** Router0's interface counters show zero carrier-change events on eth0, eth1, and eth2 since startup — confirming no link flap ever occurred. The infra_sweep found no ACL/firewall drop rules, no static ARP poisoning, no gateway divergence. The tc_snapshot found only default fq_codel qdiscs, ruling out any traffic-shaping fault. The pressure_sweep found no stress processes or resource contention on any device.

**Root cause:** No fault is present. The reported inter-department outage leaves no mechanism, no historical trace, and no current symptom — the claim is unconfirmed.

**Fix:** No corrective action is required; the network is operating correctly.
